related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of rat lungworm?

text_blocks.snippet: Rat lungworm disease, caused by the parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, can manifest with a range of symptoms, most notably severe headaches and neck stiffness, often accompanied by fever, nausea, and vomiting. Some individuals may also experience tingling or pain in the skin, and in rare cases, vision changes or paralysis. Eosinophilic meningitis, a severe form of meningitis, can also occur.
snippet_highlighted_words: severe headaches and neck stiffness, often accompanied by fever, nausea, and vomiting

list.snippet: Severe headache: This is one of the most prominent and frequently reported symptoms.
Stiff neck: Difficulty moving the neck, especially the chin towards the chest, is another common sign.
Nausea and vomiting: These gastrointestinal symptoms can be associated with the infection.
Fever: A low-grade fever may be present.
Tingling or pain in the skin: Sensations like tingling, numbness, or unusual sensitivity to pain or touch can occur.
Vision changes: Blurred vision, partial or complete blindness, or other visual disturbances can occur.
Paralysis: In rare cases, paralysis of the face or limbs may be observed.
Sensitivity to light (photophobia): Difficulty or discomfort with bright lights may be present.
Eye involvement: Larvae may migrate to the eye, causing inflammation and visual symptoms.
Eosinophilic meningitis: A severe form of meningitis characterized by the presence of eosinophils (a type of white blood cell) in the cerebrospinal fluid.

list.title: Severity varies:
list.snippet: Some people may experience mild symptoms or no symptoms at all, while others can develop severe neurological complications.

list.title: Duration of symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms typically last from a few weeks to a couple of months, but some individuals may experience longer-lasting effects.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: If you suspect you have rat lungworm disease, it's crucial to consult a healthcare professional. They may perform blood tests, imaging scans, or spinal taps to confirm the diagnosis.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment may involve medications to manage symptoms and, in some cases, specific antiparasitic drugs.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Avoid consuming raw or undercooked snails, slugs, or other potential carriers of the parasite, and thoroughly wash produce that may have come into contact with these creatures.

related_questions.question: What kills lungworm in dogs?
related_questions.snippet: Treatment to get rid of lungworms in dogs involves a dewormer that's usually administered orally for 14 days. Your dog's immune system will generate inflammation as a reaction to the dead worms and larvae, so your veterinarian may also prescribe a corticosteroid anti-inflammatory medication.
related_questions.title: Lungworms in Dogs: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, and FAQs

text_blocks.snippet: Rat lungworm disease, caused by the parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, is a serious concern for dogs, particularly in areas with snails and slugs, according to The Times of India. Dogs can contract the disease by ingesting infected snails, slugs, or even contaminated food or water. The parasite can migrate to the brain and spinal cord, leading to severe neurological issues.
snippet_highlighted_words: Dogs can contract the disease by ingesting infected snails, slugs, or even contaminated food or water

list.title: Snails and slugs:
list.snippet: Rats are the primary host, and their feces contain larvae. Snails and slugs ingest these larvae, becoming intermediate hosts. Dogs then ingest the infected snails or slugs.

list.title: Contaminated food/water:
list.snippet: Dogs can also get infected by eating food or drinking water contaminated with the larvae or the slime of infected snails/slugs, says The Times of India.
Neurological signs, such as paralysis (especially in the hind legs), abnormal pain responses, and urinary incontinence are common.
Other symptoms can include circling, seizures, and changes in behavior.
In some cases, dogs may not show any symptoms at all, or the symptoms may be mild and non-specific according to the CDC.
Control snails and slugs: Reduce their population in your yard by clearing yard clutter and using traps.
Prevent access to snails/slugs: Supervise your dog's outdoor activities and prevent them from eating snails and slugs or licking surfaces contaminated with their slime.
Clean food bowls: Ensure bowls are regularly cleaned and free of snails or slugs.
Monthly parasite control: Discuss preventative medication with your veterinarian.

list.title: Seek veterinary care immediately:
list.snippet: If you suspect your dog has rat lungworm disease, take them to a veterinarian as soon as possible. Early treatment is crucial for a positive outcome.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment may involve deworming medication and anti-inflammatory drugs, according to PetMD. In severe cases, surgery might be needed to address complications like pneumothorax (air in the chest cavity).
